newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds firmed to their strongest levels in six weeks on Monday after good offshore and local demand countered earlier jobber selling to haul yields 14 basis points lower on the day.
Shortly after 1400 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.66 percent yield from 14.80 percent overnight.

At the start, dealers said nervousness over a slightly weaker U.S. Treasury bond market triggered selling by long jobbers, which pushed the R150 up to an intraday high of 14.85 percent by around midday.
But the afternoon session was dominated by London-based demand as well as local interest.
Dealers said the offshore demand for local gilts appeared to be linked to hedging in the wake of a fresh spate of Eurorand issues, as well as J.P. Morgan's warrants on the R153 stock.

Deutsche Bank earlier launched a two billion rand 30-year zero-coupon bond, before adding one billion rand to the issue later in the day. It was followed by the World Bank, which set a 150 million rand zero-coupon bond.
J.P. Morgan also announced it had issued a total of 20,000 American-style warrants on the R153 gilt.
"We had more than three billion rands of Eurorand issues so the foreigners have had to cover and buy the stock," a dealer said.

Dealers said that fundamentally the market remained bullish, particularly as liquidity in the short-end of the market continued to improve and in the wake of slightly better-than-expected consumer inflation data on Wednesday.
Chart indicators were also extremely positive, although one trader noted the market had now reached critical technical juncture.

"The market has broken through the 15.00/14.98 percent level this week. It has spiked down but worked very hard on the way to 14.67 then retraced all the way back to the 14.80s...had a little bit of a go down again and now it is trying hard again at 14.67," a senior trader said.

"If it fails here and doesn't break down, and starts trading up towards the 80 again and then proceeds to go through it, it will be a double-bottom which could be disastrous," he said. "We could see it back at 15 pct before you blink an eyelid."
Direction in the short-term would, however, depend on the release of the Reserve Bank's March money supply and credit data at 1500 GMT on Friday.

"The key number to watch is the credit," the trader said. "If it is unchanged or a poor figure, the market will go right back up again," he said, adding that if the market met expectations, it would reinforce the market's buoyant mood.
Economists polled by Reuters have called for a 16.50 percent increase in private sector credit extension growth compared with a preliminary 17.34 percent rise in February.
Money supply growth is expected to show a 15.04 pecent year-on-year rise from February's preliminary 15.82 percent.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 464.53 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 577.02 million rand's worth on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 8.05 billion rand from 8.8 billion previously.
On the currency market, the rand also reversed its earlier weakness to trade slightly firmer late on Thursday.
It was last quoted at 4.4420/4450 against the dollar from 4.4445/4475 overnight.
The rand initially moved weaker after the market had gone short overnight in order to buy back dollars on Thursday morning for technical reasons.
That was followed by dollar selling by London-based players, linked by dealers to bond investment-related rand demand, which pushed it to a strongest level of 4.4375 bid.
At that level, dealers said importer demand resurfaced and the rand retraced to back above the 4.44 level, although traders said the currency could retry that level after the local close.
"The local guys have been holding it up...there have been natural importers all the time below 4.44," a trader said. "Once the local guys are out of the market the foreigners could push it lower."
He added that on Friday, the rand was expected to trade in a 4.43 to 4.45 range.

Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.3568/3872 yen from 28.3485/3901 yen on Wednesday, at 0.3865/3870 marks compared with 0.3854/3858 marks overnight and at 7.2227/2307 against sterling from 7.2188/2281 previously.
Money market rates were quoted little changed as the shortage held around the 7.3 billion rand level.

Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate edged lower to between 15.80 to 15.95 percent from between 15.80 to 16.00 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 7.372 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.344 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
